findings.title: Capacity meets a withdrawn medium
findings.claim: The focus's denial of the ability to seek the water becomes a relation between the seeker and the medium: when the water withdraws into depth, the agent's capacity does not suffice because the contacted provision no longer yields itself to recovery, while the same relation is echoed wherever an object or task resists access.
findings.mechanism: The carrier pair غَوْرًا and تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَبًا joins downward withdrawal to denied recovery; 18:67 and 18:72 repeat the capacity form against patience, 18:97 against the barrier, and 22:73 against a thing that cannot be recovered, allowing the root_000956/B001 yielding relation to qualify the ordinary capacity reading without replacing it.
findings.reader_payoff: Incapacity becomes newly perceptible as relational rather than as a bare shortage of will or force: the water's non-yielding withdrawal helps explain why searching cannot succeed.
findings.containment: The ordinary water, state-change, and denied-seeking readings remain intact. The obedience/yielding contact and the hidden-recess image are qualified resonances, not claims that the focus verb literally means obedience, that the water is literally a cave, or that the connected scenes form one causal sequence.

epistemic.reason: A citable trusted cross-run finding grounds the relational contact, while legacy reader-walk material and connections qualify the recurrence and the recess image; target-side morphology is not supplied for the connected ayat.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied same-surah and inter-surah connections repeat inability where patience, a barrier, or a taken object does not yield to the attempted action.
branch_activations.activation: The yielding branch contacts the focus capacity denial by making ability depend partly on whether the contacted medium or task admits the action, not only on the agent's exertion.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The failure to seek the withdrawn water includes the medium's refusal of access: desire and effort cannot make a non-yielding provision recoverable.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus verb is not replaced by a literal obedience meaning, and the connected inability scenes are not asserted to be the same event.

findings.title: Water beyond the owner's reach
findings.claim: The water's becoming غَوْرًا can be heard as a conversion of a usable garden resource into a subsurface recess, so the denied طلب names a failure of practical retrieval rather than annihilation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier غَوْرًا supplies downward withdrawal; 67:30 repeats water becoming ghawr and unavailable, 23:18 describes water settled in earth and removable, and the supplied 18:45 context returns the image to cultivated life passing into scattered remains.
findings.reader_payoff: The threat becomes spatially concrete: the resource is not merely gone, but placed where the former owner cannot reach it by searching.
findings.containment: This retains the ordinary water and failed-search readings. The cave/recess image is carried as a qualified contextual resonance, not as a claim that the water is literally a cave or that the adjacent parables are physically identical.

epistemic.reason: The wide-context reader walk supplies the two branch contacts and the spatial change, while the supplied target Arabic supports the water-loss parallels; the reader source is legacy_unbound and target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: Water as contingent provision
findings.claim: The focus water becomes newly perceptible as a provision whose accessibility depends on a source beyond the garden's possession: the same water that sustains cultivated abundance can be settled into earth, sent as a gift, made unusable, and removed.
findings.mechanism: مَاؤُهَا names the garden's water, while the supplied 23:18, 56:69, 56:70, and 71:12 connections independently frame water as sent, controlled, withdrawable, and paired with prosperity; غَوْرًا then makes that contingency local and irreversible for the seeker.
findings.reader_payoff: The garden's apparent self-sufficiency gives way to a visible dependence on a provision that remains outside its owner's control.
findings.containment: This does not identify the focus water physically with other rivers, make a broader theological claim than the supplied relations support, or replace the ordinary possessive water reading.

epistemic.reason: The focus water carrier and exact target Arabic are supplied, and the connection notes directly state the provision and withdrawal relations; target-side morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied, so the wider activation remains qualified.

findings.title: The search itself fails
findings.claim: طَلَبًا is newly legible as an active attempt to find or recover the water's location, and the focus denies that attempt's success once the supply has withdrawn.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier names seeking aimed at a concrete object; 67:30 asks who can bring accessible water after it becomes ghawr, and 22:73 describes a sought thing that cannot be recovered, returning the global retrieval failure to the focus's لَهُ طَلَبًا.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clause is felt as the collapse of a recovery operation, not merely as the owner's loss of desire or confidence.
findings.containment: The activation keeps the focus verbal noun within search and recovery; it does not extend it to debt, demand, collective seekers, or every available branch of ط ل ب.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and carrier are supplied and both target ayat have exact Arabic in the connection registry, but target-side morphology is not supplied and the cross-ayah rows remain discovery nominations.

findings.title: Entering a new condition
findings.claim: يُصْبِحَ turns the threat into an entry into a new condition: the garden's water becomes inaccessible, while wider garden scenes show cultivated abundance likewise passing into another state.
findings.mechanism: The root_000839/B010 state-change carrier at 18:41:2:1 meets the immediate 18:45 water-and-vegetation transformation and the cross-surah 68:20 garden-loss counterpart, so the focus is read as a transition rather than a static description of absence.
findings.reader_payoff: The conditional threat acquires temporal shape: what was available can become something else before the owner's recovery attempt begins.
findings.containment: The finding does not establish a strict causal order among the three أصبح clauses, does not add a transformed-owner claim, and keeps the local copular state-change reading primary.

epistemic.reason: The focus word and state-change branch are supplied, and both contextual target Arabic passages are present; the target-side morphology is not supplied and the cross-ayah links remain qualified nominations.

findings.title: Possession does not guarantee access
findings.claim: The denied ability to recover the garden's water makes apparent worldly possession a limit case for control: the nearby declaration that wealth and children are adornment becomes newly concrete when an owned resource can pass beyond the owner's reach.
findings.mechanism: The ordinary capacity branch at 18:41:6:1 is directed toward recovering the water, while 18:46 names wealth and children as temporary worldly adornment and 18:97 supplies a same-surah image of human inability before an impassable object; the relation returns through the focus's failed action.
findings.reader_payoff: The garden's visible abundance no longer reads as self-protecting ownership; its security is exposed as dependent on continued access.
findings.containment: This does not retain the unanchored HFT claim about all wealth, retinue, or autonomous power, and it does not turn the adjacent valuation into a replacement for the focus's water-loss event.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and exact 18:46/18:97 Arabic are supplied through the connection registry, but the connection rows do not supply target morphology and the broader moral extension remains bounded.
